Mineral Specimen Lot - 3 Pieces
Colemanite, Aquamarine Beryl, Pink Dolomite
Vintage, Late 20th Century
A curated collection of three distinct geological specimens, each housed in a protective acrylic display case. This lot features specimens with specific regional significance, including pieces from historic mining locations. These minerals are ideal for geology enthusiasts, educators, or collectors of natural history specimens.
Items Included:
Colemanite Specimen: Translucent crystal formation sourced from Death Valley, mounted on yellow felt.
Aquamarine Beryl: Large raw specimen dug from the mine dump at Beryl Mountain, South Acworth, N.H., dated June 24, 1977.
Pink Dolomite: Crystalline cluster from Arkansas, noted as a scarce location, mounted on burgundy felt.
Condition:
The mineral specimens themselves are in natural, raw condition with sharp crystal structures intact. The acrylic display boxes show some typical shelf wear, including light surface scuffs and dust accumulation. Original identification labels are present and legible, though some show minor age-related yellowing. The mounting adhesive and felt backings remain stable.

Hemingray, Ohio Valley Glass Co. (O.V.G. Co.)

This lot features insulators from prominent American manufacturers, showcasing the industrial aqua and teal green glass common to early 20th-century utility production. These heavy pressed glass pieces are sought after for their historical industrial aesthetic and display appeal.

Insulator, Aqua, marked "O.V.G. CO." - features a large chip on the side and base

Natural Specimen
Clear Quartz Crystal Collection
Natural and Polished Quartz Mineral
3.5" x 3.5" x 1.5" (Lot Dimensions)
Unsigned
This four-piece mineral lot features a selection of clear quartz specimens demonstrating various crystal habits and lapidary finishes. The collection includes a sharply defined double-terminated point, a large natural terminated crystal with complex internal structure, a polished point showcasing vibrant rainbow iris inclusions, and a textured rough-hewn point. These pieces illustrate the high clarity and characteristic trigonal crystal system of quartz, presenting a range of textures from pristine polished facets to raw, natural terminations.
Features one double-terminated crystal and one specimen with visible rainbow inclusions
